statement: A preselected finite session helps the chosen cohort start useful learning with little planning.
segment: Technical-learning pilot cohort to be selected
job_to_be_done: Use a short available break to make progress toward one learning goal
riskiest_assumption: Starting friction is a material reason for not learning
decision_rule: Chosen usability gate: 6 of 8 participants start and resume without moderator help; investigate consistent misunderstandings.
next_test: Observed prototype tasks comparing current navigation with a default next session
notes: 2/5/10 minutes are design options, not evidence-based optimal durations.

statement: Saved checkpoints and a bounded restart session help learners return after interruptions and missed days.
job_to_be_done: Continue a useful goal without reconstructing context or clearing a large backlog
riskiest_assumption: Reduced restart effort changes actual return behavior
decision_rule: Observe successful resume in usability tasks and self-initiated return during the pilot; keep non-return reasons.
next_test: Interruption and missed-day prototype tasks, followed by natural-use pilot
notes: Reminders, streak preference and review load must be measured separately.

statement: Recall and a fresh application prompt make short sessions more valuable than completion alone for the chosen goal.
job_to_be_done: Recall and use an idea after the original lesson
riskiest_assumption: The questions and feedback measure useful understanding without excessive effort
decision_rule: Exploratory equal-time matched-topic comparison; positive delayed-recall direction without worse fresh application, with missing follow-up reported.
next_test: Small pilot with baseline checks, delayed follow-up and rubric audit
notes: Learning studies support mechanisms in their tasks, not this product. Private recall is self-reported, not scored evidence.

statement: A simple audio mode is sufficiently useful in the selected routine to justify early mobile playback work.
segment: Learners who choose listening during travel or other suitable moments
job_to_be_done: Continue the same learning goal when reading or tapping is inconvenient
riskiest_assumption: Audio is wanted often enough and suits the selected concepts
decision_rule: Observe real mode choice and completion/return, and compare to screen-based use; do not count listening as correctness.
next_test: First-use audio, pause, transcript and resume tasks on a phone; natural-use mode diary
notes: Some people prefer rest. Technical visual tasks may need the screen. No claim that multitasking improves learning.

statement: One concrete technical-learning outcome can justify an additional paid Brainbuilder subscription.
segment: Work fluency or interview cohort, selected after discovery
job_to_be_done: Make useful progress toward an outcome worth paying to achieve
riskiest_assumption: The outcome and routine justify paying alongside established or free alternatives
decision_rule: Chosen directional gate: around 6 of 24 pilot participants choose a disclosed paid continuation; record actual commitments separately from stated intent.
next_test: Recent-purchase interviews followed by a clearly priced continuation offer after actual use
notes: No price was validated. Pilot conversion is not a market estimate. No offer or outreach has been sent.

statement: Learning from selected saved sources adds enough repeat-use value to justify scope after the core routine works.
segment: Learners with relevant articles or notes they want to revisit
job_to_be_done: Turn personally relevant material into useful practice without assembling a workflow
riskiest_assumption: Users value this over existing source-to-study products
decision_rule: Observe source selection and repeat use separately from interest; only prioritize after the core routine is usable.
next_test: Optional source-preview prototype and comparison with current workarounds
notes: Competitors already offer source import, quizzes, citations and tracking. This is not a novelty claim.
